title: ValueError: Could not interpret metric identifier: loss
body:
I am trying to implement a GridSearchCV over only a few hyperparameters but hit a block. I have spent so long combing over the Scikeras and tensorflow.keras compatibilities and just landed on using only Scikeras. There still seems to be some incompatibility issue and I don't know where.

```
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import tensorflow as tf
import keras
from keras.models import Sequential
from keras.layers import Dense
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
from scikeras.wrappers import KerasClassifier
from skopt import BayesSearchCV
from skopt.space import Real, Categorical, Integer

# ... (Your code for loading and merging DataFrames goes here) ...

# outcome_labels: Array of win/loss/draw results
outcome_labels_a = pd.read_csv('a_form.csv').T
outcome_labels_b = pd.read_csv('b_form.csv').T

# Assuming you have:
# team_a_data: DataFrame for Team A
# team_b_data: DataFrame for Team B
df_a_disposals = pd.read_csv('a_disposals.csv').T
df_a_disposals = df_a_disposals.drop(index = 'Player')
df_a_kicks = pd.read_csv('a_kicks.csv').T
df_a_kicks = df_a_kicks.drop(index = 'Player')
df_a_tackles = pd.read_csv('a_tackles.csv').T
df_a_tackles = df_a_tackles.drop(index = 'Player')
df_a_pplayed = pd.read_csv('a_pplayed.csv').T
df_a_pplayed = df_a_pplayed.drop(index = 'Player')

df_b_disposals = pd.read_csv('b_disposals.csv').T
df_b_disposals = df_b_disposals.drop(index = 'Player')
df_b_kicks = pd.read_csv('b_kicks.csv').T
df_b_kicks = df_b_kicks.drop(index = 'Player')
df_b_tackles = pd.read_csv('b_tackles.csv').T
df_b_tackles = df_b_tackles.drop(index = 'Player')
df_b_pplayed = pd.read_csv('b_pplayed.csv').T
df_b_pplayed = df_b_pplayed.drop(index = 'Player')

# Concatenate dataframes
team_a_data = pd.concat([df_a_disposals, df_a_kicks, df_a_tackles, df_a_pplayed], axis = 1)
team_b_data = pd.concat([df_b_disposals, df_b_kicks, df_b_tackles, df_b_pplayed], axis = 1)
print(team_a_data.shape)
print(team_b_data.shape)
# Combine player data for both teams
combined_data = pd.concat([team_a_data, team_b_data], axis=0)

# Merge with outcomes data
team_a_merged = pd.merge(team_a_data, outcome_labels_a, left_index = True, right_index = True)
team_b_merged = pd.merge(team_b_data, outcome_labels_b, left_index = True, right_index = True)
merged_data = pd.concat([team_a_merged, team_b_merged], axis=0)
print(team_b_merged.head())

x = merged_data.drop(columns = ['0_y'])
y = merged_data['0_y']

# Splitting initial 70%
x_train, x_remaining, y_train, y_remaining = train_test_split(x, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42) # Splitting initial 70%
# Further split remaining 30%
x_val, x_test, y_val, y_test = train_test_split(x_remaining, y_remaining, test_size=0.5, random_state=42)

# Create the model (simplifying for illustration)
def create_model(hidden_layer_dim=32, loss='binary_crossentropy', optimizer='adam', learning_rate=0.01):
    model = Sequential([
        Dense(units=32, activation='relu', input_shape=(x_train.shape[1],)), # Adjust 'units' for hidden layer size
        Dense(units=16, activation='relu'), 
        Dense(units=1, activation='sigmoid') 
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=learning_rate), 
                  loss='binary_crossentropy', 
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    
    return model

# Parameter grid
param_grid = {
    "hidden_layer_dim": [50, 100, 200],
    "loss": ["binary_crossentropy"],
    "optimizer": ["adam", "sgd"],
    "optimizer__learning_rate": [0.0001, 0.001, 0.1],
}

model = KerasClassifier(model = create_model, hidden_layer_dim=50, epochs=20, batch_size=32)

# Create a GridSearchCV object
grid = GridSearchCV(estimator=model, param_grid=param_grid, cv=3, scoring = 'accuracy')  # Consider cross-validation 

# Fit the grid search to your training data
grid_result = grid.fit(x_train, y_train)

# Best model
print(grid_result.best_params_, grid_result.best_score_)
```

comments.body:
Hi @reporter ,

It seems the source of error is from below piece of code from your error stack which is from scikeras.

```
  File "c:\Users\<user>\Code\.venv\lib\site-packages\scikeras\utils\__init__.py", line 111, in metric_name
    fn_or_cls = keras_metric_get(metric)
```

Here  `scikeras` seems passing the string `'loss' `to the argument `metric` in the above function `keras_metric_get(metric)` instead of a metric name that Keras accepts.

from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
from scikeras.wrappers import KerasClassifier
from skopt import BayesSearchCV
from skopt.space import Real, Categorical, Integer

outcome_labels_a = pd.read_csv('a_form.csv').T
outcome_labels_b = pd.read_csv('b_form.csv').T

df_a_disposals = pd.read_csv('a_disposals.csv').T

df_a_kicks = pd.read_csv('a_kicks.csv').T

df_a_tackles = pd.read_csv('a_tackles.csv').T

df_a_pplayed = pd.read_csv('a_pplayed.csv').T

df_b_disposals = pd.read_csv('b_disposals.csv').T
df_b_disposals = df_b_disposals.drop(index = 'Player')
df_b_kicks = pd.read_csv('b_kicks.csv').T
df_b_kicks = df_b_kicks.drop(index = 'Player')
df_b_tackles = pd.read_csv('b_tackles.csv').T
df_b_tackles = df_b_tackles.drop(index = 'Player')
df_b_pplayed = pd.read_csv('b_pplayed.csv').T
df_b_pplayed = df_b_pplayed.drop(index = 'Player')

team_b_data = pd.concat([df_b_disposals, df_b_kicks, df_b_tackles, df_b_pplayed], axis = 1)

team_b_merged = pd.merge(team_b_data, outcome_labels_b, left_index = True, right_index = True)

def create_model(hidden_layer_dim=32, loss='binary_crossentropy', optimizer='adam', learning_rate=0.01):
    model = Sequential([
        Dense(units=32, activation='relu', input_shape=(x_train.shape[1],)), # Adjust 'units' for hidden layer size
        Dense(units=16, activation='relu'), 
        Dense(units=1, activation='sigmoid') 
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=learning_rate), 
                  loss='binary_crossentropy', 
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    
    return model

param_grid = {
    "hidden_layer_dim": [50, 100, 200],

}

model = KerasClassifier(model = create_model, hidden_layer_dim=50, epochs=20, batch_size=32)

grid = GridSearchCV(estimator=model, param_grid=param_grid, cv=3, scoring = 'accuracy')  # Consider cross-validation

print(grid_result.best_params_, grid_result.best_score_)
